Oversight means watching over an activity or organization to make sure rules are followed and problems are caught.
Oversized Password concept
An oversized password is a password input longer than the maximum length a program can safely process.
Package Downloads concept
The process of obtaining software packages from a server for installation or updating.
package manager tool
A package manager is software that installs, updates, and manages libraries or applications for developers and operating systems.
package mirror concept
A package mirror is a server that keeps a copy of software packages so users can download them from another location.
package release concept
A package release is a published version of a software library or component that others can download and use.
PAM concept
Privileged Access Management, a set of tools and policies to secure, control, and monitor access to critical systems and data.
also: UsePAM
Paprat malware
A malware family referenced in security reporting.
Parsing technique
Breaking raw data into structured pieces so software or people can search and use it.
Password authentication technique
A login method that verifies a user by checking a password.
also: PasswordAuthentication, password logins
Password Authentication Bypass technique
A flaw or attack that lets someone log in without successfully completing normal password checks.
password field concept
A password field is an input box designed for entering a password, usually hiding the characters as they are typed.
password hashes concept
Password hashes are scrambled versions of passwords that systems store so they do not have to keep the plain passwords.
password managers tool
Password managers are apps that store and fill in passwords so users can use strong, unique passwords for different accounts.
Password Requests concept
Prompts or messages asking someone to enter, reset, or provide a password.
password-disabled accounts concept
User accounts configured so normal password authentication should not be allowed.
Patch Metadata concept
Descriptive information about a software update, such as its name, version, contents, or release details.
also: malicious patch metadata
patched concept
Patched means a software flaw has been fixed with an update.
patches concept
Patches are software updates that fix bugs, security flaws, or other problems.
patching concept
Applying software updates to fix security holes and bugs.
patient data concept
Sensitive health information about individuals, protected by laws like HIPAA, and a high-value target for ransomware and data breaches.
Patient information concept
Patient information is health-related personal data about people receiving medical care.
patient-safety concept
Patient safety is the prevention of harm to people receiving medical care.
payload concept
A payload is the part of malicious code that performs the attacker’s intended action.
payloads concept
Payloads are the parts of malware or an exploit that perform the attacker's intended action, such as stealing data or installing ransomware.
Payment details concept
Payment details are information used to pay for something, such as card numbers, billing addresses, or bank account data.
payment information concept
Payment information is data used to make purchases, such as card numbers, billing details, or payment account identifiers.
Paywall tool
An LNbits add-on that can restrict access to content or services until payment is made.
PDF product
PDF is a common document file format used to preserve how text and images appear across devices.
also: 92 KB PDF
Permissive Cross-Domain Policy Vulnerability vulnerability
A permissive cross-domain policy vulnerability is a configuration flaw that allows untrusted websites or systems to make requests they should not be allowed to make.
persistence concept
Persistence is the ability for an attacker to keep access to a system over time.
persistent access concept
Persistent access means continued access to an account or system over time.
Persistent remote access technique
Persistent remote access means an attacker keeps a way to reconnect to a system even after reboots or temporary disruptions.
Personal AI accounts concept
Personal AI accounts are privately owned accounts on AI services that employees may use outside company control.
personal data concept
Information relating to an identifiable individual, such as name, email, location, or financial details.
personal details concept
Personal details are information about a person, such as their name, address, phone number, or financial data, that can be misused if stolen.
Personal Devices concept
Phones, computers, or tablets owned by an individual rather than managed by an employer.
personal information concept
Personal information is data that can identify or describe a person, such as a name, address, phone number, or account details.
PhantomDOM tool
A browser-in-the-middle phishing tool or operation that can imitate login pages and steal active web sessions.
Phish concept
Phish is a label for a deceptive message designed to trick a recipient.
also: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
phishing technique
Phishing is a scam where attackers impersonate trusted people or services to steal information or make victims take unsafe actions.
phishing attempts technique
Phishing attempts are tries to trick people into giving up information, money, or access by pretending to be trustworthy.
phishing campaign technique
A phishing campaign is a coordinated effort to trick people into giving up passwords, money, or other sensitive information.
phishing campaigns technique
Phishing campaigns are organized attempts to trick many people into revealing information or installing malware using fake messages.
Phishing Text technique
A text message that pretends to be trustworthy to trick someone into revealing information or taking a risky action.
phone calls protocol
Phone calls are voice conversations made over telephone networks or internet calling services.
phone numbers concept
Phone numbers are the unique numbers used to reach people or devices on telephone networks.
Photos and Other Images concept
Picture files that may contain personal, business, or sensitive information.
also: images
php2shell tool
php2shell is an exploit chain referenced in security reporting that is intended to obtain command execution through PHP.
physical security concept
Physical security protects buildings, equipment, and people from real-world access, theft, or damage.
pig-butchering technique
Pig-butchering is a long-running scam where criminals build trust with a victim before tricking them into fake investments.
Ping protocol
A simple network test used to check whether another computer or service can be reached.
Ping Identity organization
A cybersecurity company that provides identity, login, and access-management products.
PingIDM product
An identity-management product for storing user data and managing accounts, logins, and access.
Pipeline concept
A pipeline is an automated sequence of steps used to build, test, or deploy software.
Plain text concept
Plain text is readable, unencrypted text that anyone with access can view directly.
Platform API Gateway product
A Jamf capability that provides a managed entry point for using platform APIs.
Pluggable Authentication Modules protocol
Pluggable Authentication Modules is a framework that lets operating systems plug in different methods for checking user logins.
pnpm tool
pnpm is a fast JavaScript package manager used to install and manage project dependencies.
also: pnpm 10
Policy enforcement concept
Policy enforcement means making sure rules, such as security or access rules, are actually applied.
politicians other
Politicians are people who hold or seek government office and may be targeted in cyber stories because of their influence or access to sensitive information.
postinstall technique
postinstall is a package script that runs automatically after software is installed, often in npm packages.
also: install-time hook, dependency `postinstall` scripts
postinstall-script technique
A postinstall script is code that runs automatically after a software package is installed, which can be abused to execute malware.
powershell
PowerShell is Microsoft’s command-line shell and scripting language, often used by administrators and abused by attackers.
also: PowerShell commands
pre-authentication concept
Pre-authentication means something happens before a user has logged in or proven who they are.
Pre-Authentication Heap-Based Buffer Overflow Vulnerability vulnerability
A pre-authentication heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability is a flaw that can let an unauthenticated attacker write too much data into a program's memory and potentially disrupt or control it.
prepare technique
An npm package lifecycle script stage that can run commands while a JavaScript package is being prepared or installed.
Pretrial detention concept
Pretrial detention is when a person is kept in custody before their trial has taken place.
Previdian organization
Previdian is a named organization, product, or service referenced in security reporting.
Private conversations concept
Messages or chats intended to be visible only to their participants or authorized users.
private key concept
A private key is secret cryptographic data used to prove identity or decrypt information and must be kept confidential.
also: secret code
private keys concept
Private keys are secret cryptographic values used to prove identity, decrypt data, or authorize cryptocurrency transactions.
Privilege escalation flaw vulnerability
A privilege escalation flaw is a vulnerability that lets someone gain more access rights than they should have.
also: priv esc vulnerability
privilege-escalation technique
Privilege escalation is when an attacker gains higher levels of access than they were supposed to have.
privileges concept
Privileges are permissions that determine what actions a user or process is allowed to perform on a system.
process injection technique
Process injection is a technique where malicious code is placed inside another running program to hide or gain its permissions.
Production Hardening technique
The process of securing a system before it is put into live use.
also: production hardening guide
Prompt concept
A prompt is the instruction or question a person gives to an AI system to guide its response.
prompting technique
Prompting is the practice of giving instructions and information to an AI model to guide its response.
Proof-of-Concept Code concept
Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
proof-of-concept exploits tool
Proof-of-concept exploits are example programs or instructions that show a security flaw can be used in practice.
proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
Public exploit code concept
Public exploit code is attack code shared openly that shows how to take advantage of a vulnerability.
Public figures concept
Public figures are well-known people, such as politicians, celebrities, or business leaders, who attract public attention.
Public reproduction labs concept
Publicly available test environments where people can try to reproduce a reported technical problem.
public services concept
Services provided by government to citizens, such as healthcare or transportation.
Publicly disclosed concept
Publicly disclosed means information has been made available for the public to know.
pull requests concept
Pull requests are proposals to merge code changes into a software project, commonly used on platforms like GitHub.
qilin
Qilin is a ransomware group that steals data and encrypts victim systems for extortion.
also: Agenda
quarantined concept
Quarantined means a suspicious file, email, or system has been isolated so it cannot easily cause harm while it is investigated.
also: quarantined on arrival, quarantine
Qubole product
A cloud data platform used to run and manage analytics workloads.
also: Qubole's platform
Queens Public Library organization
A public library system serving the Queens borough of New York City.
Queried technique
Queried means searched or requested from a database or data system using specific questions or conditions.
Qwen product
Qwen is a family of large language and AI models developed by Alibaba.
ransom note concept
A ransom note is a message telling a victim that files have been locked or data stolen and giving payment or contact instructions.
also: BYOD ransom note, README_BYOD_31.txt
ransomware concept
Ransomware is malicious software or an operation that locks or steals data to pressure victims into paying money.
ransomware activity concept
Ransomware activity is behavior related to malware that locks or steals data and demands payment from victims.
ransomware attack concept
A ransomware attack is when criminals lock files or systems and demand payment to restore access or prevent data leaks.
ransomware group threat-actor
A ransomware group is a criminal or threat-actor team that uses malware to lock or steal data and demand payment.
ransomware groups threat-actor
Ransomware groups are criminal teams that use ransomware or data theft to extort victims for money.
ransomware-as-a-service concept
Ransomware-as-a-service is a criminal business model where ransomware developers rent their malware to other attackers.
also: RaaS
real-world attacks concept
Real-world attacks are actual attempts to break into, damage, or abuse systems outside of a lab or classroom setting.
recommendation concept
A recommendation is suggested guidance or an action that someone should consider taking to reduce risk or solve a problem.
reconnaissance technique
Reconnaissance is the information-gathering step attackers use to learn about a target before trying to break in.
recovery phrase concept
A recovery phrase is a list of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet if the device or app is lost.
also: backup list of 12 or 24 words
recovery phrases concept
Recovery phrases are lists of words used to restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet or other secured account.
Recruiting concept
The act of finding and persuading people to join an organization or activity.
Red Hat Enterprise Linux product
Red Hat Enterprise Linux is a commercial Linux operating system widely used on servers and enterprise systems.
also: Red Hat
Red Hat Enterprise Linux product
Red Hat Enterprise Linux is a commercial Linux operating system for enterprise servers and workloads.
Redirected technique
Sent automatically from one website address or page to another.
redirects concept
Redirects are instructions that automatically send a user or browser from one web address to another.
Refrigeration Controllers product
Devices that monitor and control cooling equipment, including temperatures and defrost settings.
Refrigeration Controls product
Computerized systems that monitor and control refrigeration equipment such as fridges and freezers.
refrigeration equipment product
Machines and controls used to keep rooms or stored materials cold.
Refrigeration Systems product
Refrigeration systems are equipment that keep food or other goods cold at controlled temperatures.
regulators organization
Regulators are government or official bodies that create and enforce rules for industries and organizations.
release-please tool
A release-automation tool that helps software projects create version updates and release pull requests.
also: release-please pull request
remediate concept
To remediate means to fix a security problem or reduce the risk it creates.
remediation technique
Remediation is the work of fixing a security problem and reducing the damage it caused.
Remediation Guidance concept
Remediation guidance is advice on how to fix or reduce the risk from a security problem.
remote access concept
The ability to connect to another computer or network from a distant location and use it as if you were physically present.
also: unnecessary remote access, necessary remote access
remote access client tool
A remote access client is software that lets someone connect to and control another computer over a network.
remote access trojan malware
A remote access trojan is malware that secretly lets an attacker control a victim's computer from somewhere else.
remote attackers concept
Remote attackers are people who try to affect a system over a network rather than by physically accessing it.
remote command execution vulnerability
Remote command execution is when an attacker can run operating-system commands on another computer over a network.
remote control technique
Remote control means operating a computer, phone, or system from another location over a network.
Remote monitoring and management tool
Remote monitoring and management is software that lets IT staff watch and control computers or networks from afar.
also: RMM
Remote monitoring and management platform product
A remote monitoring and management platform lets IT teams manage, update, and troubleshoot computers or servers from afar.
Remote shell tool
A remote shell is command-line access to a computer over a network.
remote, unauthenticated attacker concept
A remote, unauthenticated attacker is someone who can attack over a network without first logging in.
remote-code-execution technique
Remote code execution is a serious flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from elsewhere.
also: RCE
Remotely tool
Remotely is a remote administration tool that can be used to access and manage computers over a network.
repository concept
A repository is a storage location for code, files, and their change history, especially in systems like GitHub.
Reputation concept
A trust score or history used by security systems to judge whether a sender, website, or file is likely safe.
Requirements-to-Production Workflow concept
The process of turning a requested software feature into code that is deployed for real use.
researchers organization
Researchers are people who study systems, threats, or vulnerabilities to understand and improve security.
Resource Access Certifications concept
Periodic reviews that confirm whether users or AI agents still need their existing access permissions.
Respond technique
Respond means to take action after detecting a security issue, such as containing an attack or fixing affected systems.
Restart concept
A restart is turning a device or program off and then back on again to refresh it or apply changes.
Restore technique
Restore means to bring data, settings, or a system back to an earlier working state.
retailers organization
Businesses that sell goods directly to consumers.
Revoke technique
To cancel a credential, permission, or access key so it can no longer be used.
robots concept
Robots are automated software programs, often called bots, that perform tasks on the internet without a human clicking each step.
romance baiting technique
Romance baiting is a scam where criminals build a fake romantic relationship to gain trust and then push the victim into sending money or investing.
root concept
The superuser account on Unix and Linux systems that has unlimited control over the entire computer.
root access concept
Having complete administrative control over a computer or network, allowing unrestricted system changes.
root cause concept
Root cause means the underlying reason a problem or security incident happened, not just its visible symptoms.
root privileges concept
Root privileges are the highest level of control on Unix-like systems, allowing a user or program to change almost anything.
root-level concept
Root-level means having the highest level of control over a device or operating system.
Routines product
A Jamf capability for automating recurring device-management tasks.
runtime concept
Runtime is the period when a program is actively running, or the software environment it needs in order to run.
runtime enforcement technique
A security technique that monitors and enforces policies during the execution of a program, blocking violations in real-time.
russia
Russia is a country frequently referenced in cybersecurity stories involving cybercrime groups, espionage, and government activity.
also: Russian, Russia-based
Rust tool
Rust is a programming language often used to build fast and memory-safe software, including security tools and malware.
S3 product
S3 is Amazon’s cloud object-storage service, often used to store files, backups, logs, and website data.
also: S3 buckets, buckets
S3 Data Events concept
AWS CloudTrail records that show access to individual files and objects stored in Amazon S3.
S3 server access logs product
S3 server access logs are records of requests made to Amazon S3 storage buckets.
SaaS concept
SaaS is software delivered over the internet as a subscription or hosted service instead of installed and managed entirely by the customer.
sabotage technique
Sabotage is deliberate damage or disruption meant to weaken an organization, system, or country.
Safari product
Apple's web browser that comes pre-installed on Macs, iPhones, and iPads.
SafeDep organization
SafeDep appears to be a security company or product focused on software supply chain risks.
Safety training concept
Safety training teaches people how to avoid harm, handle risks, and follow safe procedures.
SAM product
SAM, or Security Account Manager, is a Windows database that stores local user account and password-related information.
SAML protocol
SAML is a standard that lets users sign in once and access multiple services by passing trusted identity messages between them.
also: SAML authentication controls
SAML authentication protocol
SAML authentication is a single sign-on method that lets one service trust another service to confirm a user's identity.
SAML authentication bypass technique
A flaw or attack that lets someone get around login checks based on Security Assertion Markup Language authentication.
sanctioned concept
Sanctioned means officially restricted or penalized by a government, often by banning business dealings or freezing assets.
sanctions concept
Government-imposed restrictions that block or limit trade, financial dealings, or travel with targeted individuals or countries.
sanctions evasion concept
Sanctions evasion is trying to get around government restrictions placed on people, companies, or countries.
Satoshis concept
The smallest standard unit of Bitcoin, with 100 million satoshis equal to one bitcoin.
Saudi government organization
The national government of Saudi Arabia.
Saudi military organization
The armed forces of Saudi Arabia.
Saudi Royal Family organization
The ruling royal family of Saudi Arabia.
Scam technique
A scam is a dishonest scheme designed to trick people into giving up money, information, or access.
Scam Call Centers concept
Operations that use phone calls to trick people into sending money or revealing personal information.
scam centers organization
Scam centers are organized workplaces where criminals run fraud schemes, often using phones, messaging apps, or fake websites.
Scam messages concept
Scam messages are texts, emails, or chats designed to trick people into sending money, data, or access.
scammers threat-actor
Scammers are people who trick others to steal money, information, or access.
scams concept
Scams are dishonest schemes designed to trick people into giving money, information, or access.
scanner tool
A scanner is a tool that searches for information or problems automatically.
scans concept
Scans are automated checks that examine software or related data for issues or information.
scheduled task technique
A scheduled task is a job set to run automatically at a certain time or under certain conditions.
scheduled-tasks
Scheduled tasks are automated jobs on a computer that attackers can abuse to run malware at specific times or after reboot.
scheduler tool
A scheduler is a system component that runs tasks automatically at chosen times or intervals.
also: built-in scheduler
Schneider Electric organization
Schneider Electric is a major industrial technology company whose products are used in energy management, automation, and critical infrastructure.
Schneider Electric Equipment product
Industrial and energy-management equipment made by Schneider Electric.
SCL concept
SCL is a spam confidence level score used to help decide how suspicious an email is.
also: SCL 1
scope concept
scope defines what access, targets, or permissions are included in a security test, login request, or authorization grant.
screenconnect
ScreenConnect, now ConnectWise Control, is a remote-support tool that attackers sometimes abuse for unauthorized access.
also: ScreenConnect Client, ScreenConnect 25.4.3, ScreenConnect Client (5cbe79c9c25524df)
screenshot concept
A screenshot is a captured image of what is shown on a screen.
screenshot capture technique
Screenshot capture is the act of taking an image of what is currently shown on a device's screen.
screenshots concept
Images that capture what is currently shown on a computer screen.
scripts tool
Scripts are small sets of commands that automate tasks a computer should perform.
also: small scripts
Secrets Manager product
Secrets Manager usually refers to a cloud service for storing and rotating sensitive values such as passwords, tokens, and API keys.
Security alert concept
A security alert is a notification that something potentially suspicious or dangerous was detected.
Security Analyst concept
A security analyst is a role focused on reviewing security-related information and findings.
Security awareness concept
Knowing about common cyber risks and safer ways to use technology.
Security fixes concept
Security fixes are software updates that repair weaknesses attackers could exploit.
security flaw vulnerability
A security flaw is a weakness in software, hardware, or a process that attackers could use to cause harm.
also: security issue
Security incidents concept
Security incidents are events that threaten the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of systems or data.
security professionals concept
Security professionals are people whose job is to protect systems, data, and organizations from security threats.
security researchers organization
Security researchers are people who study systems, software, and attacks to find vulnerabilities and improve defenses.
Security Service of Ukraine organization
The main intelligence and law enforcement agency of Ukraine, involved in counter-intelligence and cyber defense.
Security testers concept
People who examine systems to find and verify security weaknesses.
Security Warnings concept
Alerts that tell users about a possible security risk or unsafe action.
Securotrop threat-actor
A threat-actor operation referenced in security reporting.
Seed Phrase concept
A seed phrase is a list of secret words that can restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet.
seed phrases concept
Seed phrases are lists of words that can restore access to a cryptocurrency wallet, so stealing them can steal the funds.
SEGA organization
A Japanese video-game and entertainment company.
SEGA Account product
SEGA's online account service for users of its games and services.
SEGA Fave organization
A SEGA-affiliated organization that operates arcade-game and entertainment services.
SEGA ID product
A user identity and registration service for SEGA online services.
SEGA Lucky Kuji Online product
SEGA's online service for lottery-style merchandise promotions.
seizure concept
A law-enforcement action that takes control of criminally used property, domains, or infrastructure.
sender concept
A sender is the person, account, server, or system that sends a message such as an email.
sender reputation concept
Sender reputation is a trust score email systems use to judge whether messages from a sender are likely safe or spam.
sensitive credentials concept
Important login information, such as passwords, private keys, or security tokens, that should be protected.
sensitive data concept
Sensitive data is information that could cause harm if exposed, such as passwords, financial details, or medical records.
sensitive files concept
Sensitive files are files that contain private, secret, or valuable information that should not be exposed to unauthorized people.
sensitive information concept
Sensitive information is data that should be protected because exposing it could harm a person, company, or system.
Sensitive records concept
Sensitive records are stored pieces of information that could harm people or organizations if exposed.
Sentra organization
A data security company that helps organizations discover and protect sensitive cloud data.
server data concept
Server data is information stored, processed, or logged by a computer that provides services to users or other systems.
Server Files concept
Files stored on a server, such as application code, settings, logs, or user data.
servers tool
Servers are computers that provide services, websites, or data to other computers over a network.
Service Desk concept
A service desk is a support team that handles user requests, technical issues, and account help.

A service disruption is a period when an online service is unavailable, slow, or not working correctly for users.

A software feature that brings service settings or data into a system from another source.

A session is a period of activity where a user or program is logged in or connected to a service.

A session validation vulnerability is a flaw that may let someone use, alter, or bypass a logged-in session without proper checks.

The process of preparing a device, application, or account for use.
SHA-crypt protocol
A password-hashing method that uses the SHA family of cryptographic algorithms to store passwords more safely.
also: SHA-crypt (5 or 6) hash
Shadow AI Agent Discovery for Endpoints product
A security capability for finding AI agents running on employee devices without approved oversight.
Shahid Kaveh threat-actor
A threat-actor unit publicly attributed to Iranian cyber operations.
Shahid Shoostari threat-actor
A threat-actor unit referenced in reporting on Iranian cyber operations.
Shared Hosting concept
A web-hosting service where multiple customers' websites share the same server and resources.
shinyhunters
ShinyHunters is a cybercrime group known for stealing and selling large databases of user information.
Shochiku Multiplex Theatres organization
A Japanese cinema-chain organization.
Sign-In concept
Sign-in is the process of proving your identity to access a computer, account, or online service.
Signal product
A privacy-focused messaging app that encrypts calls and messages end-to-end, meaning only the sender and receiver can read them.
signing technique
A cryptographic process that uses a private key to prove that data came from its owner and was not changed.
SIM cards product
SIM cards are small chips that identify a mobile phone account to a cellular network.
SIXZUT malware
A Linux rootkit malware family designed to hide malicious files, processes, and network activity.
also: a ring 3 rootkit
sleepyduck malware
A malware family referenced in security reporting.
also: SleepyDuck / EtherDuck
SlippyNunchucks threat-actor
A China-aligned threat-actor group referenced in security reporting.
SLSA provenance concept
SLSA provenance is tamper-resistant information about how software was built, used to help verify that the software supply chain has not been compromised.
also: valid SLSA provenance
social engineering technique
Social engineering is manipulation of people into doing something or sharing information they otherwise would not.
social engineering attacks technique
Social engineering attacks are tricks that manipulate people into revealing information or doing something unsafe.
also: social-engineering attempts
social engineering fraud technique
Social engineering fraud is a scam that manipulates people into sending money, sharing secrets, or taking unsafe actions.
social engineering scams technique

social media concept
Social media means online platforms where people share messages, photos, videos, and other content.

Social media accounts are online profiles on platforms like Instagram, X, Facebook, or TikTok that attackers may try to steal or impersonate.

Social Security numbers are U.S. government identification numbers often targeted by criminals because they can be used for fraud.

software supply-chain compromise concept
A software supply-chain compromise is an attack where trusted software, updates, packages, or build systems are tampered with to reach users.
Software Update concept
A newer version of software that may add improvements or fix problems and security flaws.
Sogou Input Method product
A Chinese-language typing application that helps users enter text on computers.
Soldiers of Solomon threat-actor
An online identity associated with a threat actor in security reporting.
solidity-langsupport-runner.service other
A Linux system service definition file, which can be used to automatically start a program and keep it running.
SonicOS product

SonicOS Management Interface product
The SonicOS management interface is the web-based administrative interface for configuring SonicWall security appliances.
SonicOS SSL VPN product
A SonicWall remote-access service that uses SSL/TLS to let users connect securely to a private network.
SonicWall organization
SonicWall is a cybersecurity vendor known for firewalls, secure remote access, and network security products.
SonicWall firewalls product
SonicWall firewalls are network security devices that inspect and control traffic entering or leaving a network.
SonicWall Global Management System product
SonicWall Global Management System is a product used to centrally manage SonicWall network security devices.
SonicWall Network Security Manager product
SonicWall Network Security Manager is a product used to centrally manage SonicWall network security devices.
source IP concept
A source IP is the internet address a network request appears to come from.
Sources and methods concept
Sources and methods are the people, tools, and techniques intelligence services use to collect information.
spearphishing-link
A spearphishing link is a targeted phishing message that includes a malicious link tailored to a specific person or organization.
Specialized Services concept
For-hire services that provide a particular capability, such as technical support, access, or fraud assistance.

SQL injection technique
SQL injection is a web attack where malicious database commands are inserted into an application's input fields or requests.
SSH protocol

SSH access protocol
Remote access to a computer using Secure Shell, an encrypted network administration protocol.
SSH keys protocol
SSH keys are cryptographic login credentials used to securely access remote computers and services.

SSH password authentication is a remote-login method that verifies a user with a password over an encrypted SSH connection.
SSH Services protocol
Network services that use Secure Shell to provide encrypted remote command-line access to devices.

sshd logs concept
Records created by the SSH server that show connection and login activity.

A named security vulnerability affecting some OpenSSH password-authentication setups.
SSL protocol
A protocol once widely used to encrypt data between a device and a website, now mostly replaced by TLS.
SSL VPN protocol

SSL-VPN Service protocol
An SSL-VPN service lets people securely connect to a private network remotely through an encrypted internet connection.

SSO concept
